svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Resource Explorer answers the untagged-resource question that a tag policy cannot see, using a tag:none query, but it returns results from one of two index types and the output does not say which. Resource Explorer-owned indexes provide immediate partial results, covering all tagged resources and supported untagged resources created after the immediate resource discovery release, and require only the read-only managed policy. User-owned indexes provide complete results with automatic updates and additionally require the iam colon CreateServiceLinkedRole permission, after which any later user gets complete results with read-only permissions alone. For a query whose purpose is finding untagged resources, the population most likely to be missing from partial results is the untagged resources that have existed longest. The diagram also shows three separate scopes each with its own enablement: the current Region by default since 6 October 2025, all Regions by selecting an aggregator Region, and all accounts through Organizations trusted access and a CloudFormation deployment. Resource Explorer is eventually consistent, so finding a resource in one Region and replicating it to the aggregator index takes time. Its quotas cannot be increased and include ten views per Region and five search operations per second.
svg.title: Two calibrations, one output format
svg.text: The same query, two populations, and the result does not say which.
“To find untagged resources in your account, use AWS Resource Explorer with a query that uses tag:none.”
RESOURCE EXPLORER-OWNED INDEX
“immediate partial results”
“all tagged resources and supported untagged
resources created after the immediate resource
discovery release”
needs: AWSResourceExplorerReadOnlyAccess
USER-OWNED INDEX
“complete results with automatic updates”
The inventory.
needs also: iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
Once, by anyone. After that, read-only is enough.
Read the parenthesis against the thing you are searching for
Tagged resources: all of them. Untagged resources: only those created after a particular release.
So the untagged resources most likely to be missing are the ones that have been sitting there longest.
Three scopes, three separate enablements — one query, three different numbers
current Region default since 6 Oct 2025, “no setup steps required”
all Regions select an aggregator Region
all accounts Organizations trusted access + CloudFormation deployment
And the aggregated view lags
“eventually consistent” — finding a resource in one
Region and replicating it to the aggregator index
“can take some time”.
Quotas are hard
“You cannot increase the quotas for AWS Resource
Explorer.” 10 views per Region, 5 searches per second
— ample for a person, tight for a nightly sweep.
Write down what the number counted, over what scope, at what time, and under which index.
An inventory is what every other number gets compared against, so one that is quietly partial does not
produce one wrong answer — it produces a baseline, and nobody re-derives a baseline.
Pairs with #104: the tag policy counts tags that are wrong; tag:none counts resources with none at all.
